input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view in the Dashboard (side-by-side and diff)

## Description

This epic delivers the core run comparison capability in the Dashboard: users can select two or more training/pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side, and, for two selected runs, a diff presentation that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between them. This replaces the current workflow where comparison happens only in exported spreadsheets because parameters and metrics live in per-run pages.

## Scope

- Add multi-run selection from the existing runs list in the Dashboard (two or more runs).
- Render a comparison view showing parameters and metrics of the selected runs side by side.
- Provide a diff presentation mode of the same comparison surface that highlights which parameters and metrics differ between two selected runs (the diff is a mode of the comparison view over the same run data, not a separate surface).
- Read run parameters and metrics through the existing run data surfaces the Dashboard already uses for per-run pages; no new backend data plane is introduced by this epic.
- Validation that the comparison view works against Data Science Pipelines runs (parameters and metrics for multiple runs retrievable and rendered correctly), recorded as an acceptance criterion on this epic's deliverable.
- Incidental UI text and in-product reference updates that fall out of the new views are included here; standalone documentation is handled separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a list of runs, when the user selects two or more runs, then a comparison view opens showing each run's parameters and metrics side by side.
- Given two selected runs in the comparison view, when the user switches to the diff presentation, then the parameters and metrics that differ between the two runs are highlighted, and unchanged values are distinguishable from changed ones.
- Given runs produced by Data Science Pipelines, when compared, then their parameters and metrics are retrieved via the existing pipeline run surfaces and rendered completely in both presentation modes (validates the Data Science Pipelines component keeps working with this feature).
- The comparison view is reachable from the runs list in the Dashboard without leaving the platform (no spreadsheet export required for comparison).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard — fully covered by this epic.
- HLR-3 (P1): Run "diff" view highlighting which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs — covered by this epic. Consolidated with HLR-1: both describe the same comparison surface over the same run data for the same component and team (the strategy notes wording overlap kept from two customer councils); the diff is a presentation mode of the side-by-side view, so splitting would build the same UI surface twice. Bundled at the higher priority (P0).

# Link registered model versions to producing runs

## Description

This epic delivers the Model Registry side of run lineage: registered model versions record a link back to the run that produced them, so that the run (and its parameters and metrics) can be identified from a registered model version and a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. The linkage uses the registry's existing extension point for structured metadata on model versions.

## Scope

- Define and record the linkage from a registered model version to the run that produced it, using the existing model version metadata extension point (custom properties on ModelVersion entities exposed via the registry REST API).
- Make the linkage available through the registry's existing REST API so consuming UIs can resolve the producing run for a model version.
- Apply the linkage when model versions are registered from runs (the producing run is captured as part of registration).
- No Dashboard UI changes in this epic; surfacing the link in the UI is handled by the Dashboard team separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a run, when the model version is read via the registry REST API, then the run that produced it is identifiable from the model version's metadata.
- Given a model version with run linkage, when the linkage is resolved, then it points at a run that is accessible in the same project context (parameters and metrics of that run retrievable through existing run surfaces).
- The linkage mechanism uses the existing model version metadata extension point and does not require a new registry data model migration beyond that extension point.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry — registry-side half covered by this epic (the Dashboard-side surfacing is a separate epic owned by the Dashboard team).

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry UI

## Description

This epic delivers the Dashboard-side surfacing of model-version run lineage: from the Model Registry UI in the Dashboard, a user can see the run that produced a registered model version and open the run comparison view starting from that run. This connects the registry catalog to the comparison capability so promotion decisions can be made without leaving the platform.

## Scope

- Surface the producing-run linkage on registered model version views in the Dashboard's Model Registry UI.
- Add an entry point from a registered model version to the run comparison view (e.g., open a comparison seeded with the producing run so another run can be selected to compare against).
- Build against the model-version-to-run linkage exposed by the Model Registry REST API and extend the existing run comparison view; do not build a second comparison surface.
- Incidental UI text updates that fall out of these changes are included here; standalone documentation is handled separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that has a producing-run link, when the user views it in the Model Registry UI, then the producing run is visible and identifiable.
- Given a registered model version with a producing-run link, when the user opens a comparison from it, then the run comparison view opens with the producing run selected so a second run can be chosen for comparison.
- Given a registered model version without a producing-run link (legacy registrations), when viewed, then the comparison entry point degrades gracefully without errors.
- The entry point reuses the existing run comparison view rather than duplicating it.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry — Dashboard-side half covered by this epic (registry-side linkage is a separate epic owned by the Model Registry team).

# Validate multi-run parameter/metric retrieval for Data Science Pipelines

## Description

This epic delivers a validation of the Data Science Pipelines component as it supports the new run comparison capability: confirm that parameters and metrics for multiple pipeline runs can be retrieved through the existing pipeline run surfaces in the way the Dashboard comparison view consumes them, and report any gaps. Data Science Pipelines requires no code changes for the comparison feature per the strategy; this epic is the validation work performed by the component's owning team because a different team owns the component than the one building the comparison UI.

## Scope

- Exercise retrieval of parameters and metrics for multiple runs (including runs from different experiments where applicable within a project) through the existing run data surfaces the Dashboard uses.
- Confirm the retrieved data is complete and correctly attributed per run for side-by-side and diff presentation (parameters and metric values match what the per-run pages show).
- Produce a findings report: confirmed behaviors, and any gaps or limitations discovered (with severity), handed to the Dashboard team.
- If a gap is found that would require a Data Science Pipelines code change, record it as a finding for follow-up planning; implementing such a change is out of scope for this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation report exists covering retrieval of parameters and metrics for multiple pipeline runs through the existing run surfaces, with a clear pass/fail conclusion per checked behavior.
- Parameters and metric values retrieved for a set of runs match the values shown on the corresponding per-run pages (no missing or misattributed values).
- Any gaps or limitations discovered are documented with severity and a recommended follow-up, and communicated to the Dashboard team.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0) / HLR-3 (P1) (supporting validation): the comparison view's correctness against Data Science Pipelines runs is confirmed by this epic; the comparison feature itself is built by the Dashboard team.

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

This epic delivers user documentation for the run comparison workflow: how to compare training and pipeline runs side by side and as a diff from the runs list, and how to open a comparison from the Model Registry via a registered model version's producing-run link.

## Scope

- New documentation topics covering:
  - Selecting two or more runs from the runs list and viewing their parameters and metrics side by side.
  - Using the diff presentation to see which parameters and metrics changed between two runs.
  - Opening a comparison from the Model Registry, starting from a registered model version's producing-run link.
  - Guidance on using comparison for model promotion decisions (within the documented workflow; automatic selection/promotion is out of scope).
- Follow the Red Hat docs content process and tooling for authoring and publishing these topics.
- Accuracy validation against the implemented behavior of the comparison view, the registry linkage, and the registry entry point.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers the comparison workflow from both entry points: the runs list and the Model Registry.
- The documented steps match the implemented behavior, technically reviewed against the implementation by the owning engineering teams.
- The diff presentation and the registry-initiated comparison are each documented with a walkthrough a data scientist can follow end to end.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry — fully covered by this epic.
